replies.author: Mammoth-Drawing-6939
replies.body:
I don't think the Performance Settings are working correctly. It almost seems to make it run worse? I'm not sure it's the graphics that are the issue, I think it's the entities spawning, calculations/timers for traps, rest of game logic etc etc.

This took me quite a few plays to understand what the gameplay is supposed to be like. What I figured is that I sort of stay near the spawn area and lay traps (didn't even realize I could place turrets for a while) but that works pretty terribly. Really the way to play is the keep making loops around the street near the spawn area and drop traps along the way. I think you need to change some things gameplay wise...

First of all, if meta-progression is the way to make this game easier, don't make that resource be the banked gold. That discourages spending your gold for resources during gameplay to save enough to upgrade permanently. It's a sort of "don't play the game to get better at the game" thing. Playing a round, no matter how well I (in general), should get me some sort of experience towards my next meta-progression upgrade.

The bazooka fires way too slow and you have to get lucky with supply drops to make that any better. That needs to sped up by default. Maybe sometimes I want to blow up houses for resources, but I can't do that with a near 4 second cooldown; I have to run away by then. Look at other roguelites: your typical default attack is much faster and you can upgrade it so much sooner, as well as adding more new weapons to your arsenal early in the game. Consider an option for auto-aim or not as well.

5 gold for the cheapest temporary trap is absurd. Gold is hard to pick up sometimes so you just get screwed after a while if most of your traps are gone. Spike trap should honestly be like 1 or 2 gold max. The rest of the traps should be lowered as well.

Add an option to spend gold to heal in the traps menu or something. That would be a good use of 5/10 gold and that decision would be a fun balancing choice for players. Or have enemies drop health packs sometimes. 

Pickup range is too small by default, and I don't think having the resources bounce away with physics is a good choice at all. **That might be a part of your performance issue.** Just have those drop at the enemies' feet when they die. 

Sometimes you can't see the zombies behind houses, and it seems like they can either completely clip thru the houses or pretty far into them which makes it super unfair. 

Enemies might need a sort of tiny delay on their player tracking? They just change direction so quick you can't juke them out at all.

The robot dog is real bullshit and I can never tell where his missile is about to go. It should be obvious from the beginning. Wave 4 seems so early to spawn a boss too. I barely have any upgrades or traps/turrets placed by the time he comes in.

Add some colorblindness settings. On Performance Mode especially it's super hard to tell coins from exp.

It's not obvious enough when you get hit by an enemy. I still think you need to fix the UI for health as well. Maybe have the hearts or health bar floating over the player character.

Panic Rune is useless without a +1 health increase supply drop or permanent progression. You should change that to 33% or lower health so it works if you're at 1/3 hearts.

The running zombies are too fast to start. If they sped up (slowly) over waves or had an acceleration system or something when they had to change direction that would help.

Overall I think your idea of the game could be really good, it just needs a lot of balancing to actually show your vision.
